work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Dead March. Enter the funeral of King Henry the Fifth, attended on by the Duke of Bedford, Regent of France; the Duke of Gloucester, Protector; the Duke of Exeter, the Earl of Warwick, the Bishop of Winchester, the Duke of Somerset with Heralds, &c.

lines.text: Hung be the heavens with black, yield day to night!
lines.plainText: Hung be the heavens with black yield day to night

lines.text: Comets, importing change of times and states,
lines.plainText: Comets importing change of times and states

lines.text: Brandish your crystal tresses in the sky,
lines.plainText: Brandish your crystal tresses in the sky

lines.text: And with them scourge the bad revolting stars
lines.plainText: And with them scourge the bad revolting stars

lines.text: That have consented unto Henry's death:
lines.plainText: That have consented unto Henry's death

lines.text: King Henry the Fifth, too famous to live long!
lines.plainText: King Henry the Fifth too famous to live long

lines.text: England ne'er lost a king of so much worth.
lines.plainText: England ne'er lost a king of so much worth

lines.text: England ne'er had a king until his time.
lines.plainText: England ne'er had a king until his time

lines.text: Virtue he had, deserving to command;
lines.plainText: Virtue he had deserving to command

lines.text: His brandish'd sword did blind men with his beams;
lines.plainText: His brandish'd sword did blind men with his beams

lines.text: His arms spread wider than a dragon's wings;
lines.plainText: His arms spread wider than a dragon's wings

lines.text: His sparkling eyes, replete with wrathful fire,
lines.plainText: His sparkling eyes replete with wrathful fire

lines.text: More dazzled and drove back his enemies
lines.plainText: More dazzled and drove back his enemies

lines.text: Than mid-day sun fierce bent against their faces.
lines.plainText: Than midday sun fierce bent against their faces

lines.text: What should I say? His deeds exceed all speech.
lines.plainText: What should I say His deeds exceed all speech

lines.text: He ne'er lift up his hand but conquered.
lines.plainText: He ne'er lift up his hand but conquered

lines.text: We mourn in black; why mourn we not in blood?
lines.plainText: We mourn in black why mourn we not in blood

lines.text: Henry is dead and never shall revive.
lines.plainText: Henry is dead and never shall revive

lines.text: Upon a wooden coffin we attend,
lines.plainText: Upon a wooden coffin we attend

lines.text: And Death's dishonourable victory
lines.plainText: And Death's dishonourable victory

lines.text: We with our stately presence glorify,
lines.plainText: We with our stately presence glorify

lines.text: Like captives bound to a triumphant car.
lines.plainText: Like captives bound to a triumphant car

lines.text: What! Shall we curse the planets of mishap
lines.plainText: What Shall we curse the planets of mishap

lines.text: That plotted thus our glory's overthrow?
lines.plainText: That plotted thus our glory's overthrow

lines.text: Or shall we think the subtle-witted French
lines.plainText: Or shall we think the subtlewitted French

lines.text: Conjurers and sorcerers, that, afraid of him,
lines.plainText: Conjurers and sorcerers that afraid of him

lines.text: By magic verses have contriv'd his end?
lines.plainText: By magic verses have contriv'd his end

lines.text: He was a king bless'd of the King of kings;
lines.plainText: He was a king bless'd of the King of kings

lines.text: Unto the French the dreadful judgement-day
lines.plainText: Unto the French the dreadful judgementday

lines.text: So dreadful will not be as was his sight.
lines.plainText: So dreadful will not be as was his sight

lines.text: The battles of the Lord of Hosts he fought:
lines.plainText: The battles of the Lord of Hosts he fought

lines.text: The Church's prayers made him so prosperous.
lines.plainText: The Church's prayers made him so prosperous

lines.text: The Church! Where is it? Had not churchmen pray'd,
lines.plainText: The Church Where is it Had not churchmen pray'd

lines.text: His thread of life had not so soon decay'd.
lines.plainText: His thread of life had not so soon decay'd

lines.text: None do you like but an effeminate prince,
lines.plainText: None do you like but an effeminate prince

lines.text: Whom like a school-boy you may overawe.
lines.plainText: Whom like a schoolboy you may overawe

lines.text: Gloucester, whate'er we like, thou art Protector,
lines.plainText: Gloucester whate'er we like thou art Protector

lines.text: And lookest to command the Prince and realm.
lines.plainText: And lookest to command the Prince and realm

lines.text: Thy wife is proud; she holdeth thee in awe
lines.plainText: Thy wife is proud she holdeth thee in awe

lines.text: More than God or religious churchmen may.
lines.plainText: More than God or religious churchmen may

lines.text: Name not religion, for thou lov'st the flesh,
lines.plainText: Name not religion for thou lov'st the flesh

lines.text: And ne'er throughout the year to church thou go'st,
lines.plainText: And ne'er throughout the year to church thou go'st

lines.text: Except it be to pray against thy foes.
lines.plainText: Except it be to pray against thy foes

lines.text: Cease, cease these jars, and rest your minds in peace;
lines.plainText: Cease cease these jars and rest your minds in peace

lines.text: Let's to the altar; heralds, wait on us.
lines.plainText: Let's to the altar heralds wait on us

lines.text: Instead of gold, we'll offer up our arms,
lines.plainText: Instead of gold we'll offer up our arms

lines.text: Since arms avail not, now that Henry's dead.
lines.plainText: Since arms avail not now that Henry's dead

lines.text: Posterity, await for wretched years,
lines.plainText: Posterity await for wretched years

lines.text: When at their mothers' moist eyes babes shall suck,
lines.plainText: When at their mothers' moist eyes babes shall suck

lines.text: Our isle be made a nourish of salt tears,
lines.plainText: Our isle be made a nourish of salt tears

lines.text: And none but women left to wail the dead.
lines.plainText: And none but women left to wail the dead

lines.text: Henry the Fifth, thy ghost I invocate:
lines.plainText: Henry the Fifth thy ghost I invocate

lines.text: Prosper this realm, keep it from civil broils,
lines.plainText: Prosper this realm keep it from civil broils

lines.text: Combat with adverse planets in the heavens.
lines.plainText: Combat with adverse planets in the heavens

lines.text: A far more glorious star thy soul will make
lines.plainText: A far more glorious star thy soul will make

lines.text: Than Julius Caesar or bright—
lines.plainText: Than Julius Caesar or bright

lines.text: My honourable lords, health to you all!
lines.plainText: My honourable lords health to you all

lines.text: Sad tidings bring I to you out of France,
lines.plainText: Sad tidings bring I to you out of France

lines.text: Of loss, of slaughter, and discomfiture:
lines.plainText: Of loss of slaughter and discomfiture

lines.text: Guienne, Champaigne, Rheims, Rouen, Orleans,
lines.plainText: Guienne Champaigne Rheims Rouen Orleans

lines.text: Paris, Guysors, Poictiers, are all quite lost.
lines.plainText: Paris Guysors Poictiers are all quite lost

lines.text: What say'st thou, man, before dead Henry's corse?
lines.plainText: What say'st thou man before dead Henry's corse

lines.text: Speak softly, or the loss of those great towns
lines.plainText: Speak softly or the loss of those great towns

lines.text: Will make him burst his lead and rise from death.
lines.plainText: Will make him burst his lead and rise from death

lines.text: Is Paris lost? Is Rouen yielded up?
lines.plainText: Is Paris lost Is Rouen yielded up

lines.text: If Henry were recall'd to life again,
lines.plainText: If Henry were recall'd to life again

lines.text: These news would cause him once more yield the ghost.
lines.plainText: These news would cause him once more yield the ghost

lines.text: How were they lost? What treachery was us'd?
lines.plainText: How were they lost What treachery was us'd

lines.text: No treachery, but want of men and money.
lines.plainText: No treachery but want of men and money

lines.text: Amongst the soldiers this is muttered:
lines.plainText: Amongst the soldiers this is muttered

lines.text: That here you maintain several factions
lines.plainText: That here you maintain several factions

lines.text: And whilst a field should be dispatch'd and fought,
lines.plainText: And whilst a field should be dispatch'd and fought

lines.text: You are disputing of your generals.
lines.plainText: You are disputing of your generals

lines.text: One would have lingering wars with little cost;
lines.plainText: One would have lingering wars with little cost

lines.text: Another would fly swift, but wanteth wings;
lines.plainText: Another would fly swift but wanteth wings

lines.text: A third thinks, without expense at all,
lines.plainText: A third thinks without expense at all

lines.text: By guileful fair words peace may be obtain'd.
lines.plainText: By guileful fair words peace may be obtain'd

lines.text: Awake, awake, English nobility!
lines.plainText: Awake awake English nobility

lines.text: Let not sloth dim your honours new-begot.
lines.plainText: Let not sloth dim your honours newbegot

lines.text: Cropp'd are the flower-de-luces in your arms;
lines.plainText: Cropp'd are the flowerdeluces in your arms

lines.text: Of England's coat one half is cut away.
lines.plainText: Of England's coat one half is cut away

lines.text: Were our tears wanting to this funeral,
lines.plainText: Were our tears wanting to this funeral

lines.text: These tidings would call forth their flowing tides.
lines.plainText: These tidings would call forth their flowing tides

lines.text: Me they concern; Regent I am of France.
lines.plainText: Me they concern Regent I am of France

lines.text: Give me my steeled coat. I'll fight for France.
lines.plainText: Give me my steeled coat I'll fight for France

lines.text: Away with these disgraceful wailing robes!
lines.plainText: Away with these disgraceful wailing robes

lines.text: Wounds will I lend the French instead of eyes,
lines.plainText: Wounds will I lend the French instead of eyes

lines.text: To weep their intermissive miseries.
lines.plainText: To weep their intermissive miseries

lines.text: Lords, view these letters full of bad mischance.
lines.plainText: Lords view these letters full of bad mischance

lines.text: France is revolted from the English quite,
lines.plainText: France is revolted from the English quite

lines.text: Except some petty towns of no import.
lines.plainText: Except some petty towns of no import

lines.text: The Dauphin Charles is crowned king in Rheims;
lines.plainText: The Dauphin Charles is crowned king in Rheims

lines.text: The Bastard of Orleans with him is join'd;
lines.plainText: The Bastard of Orleans with him is join'd

lines.text: Reignier, Duke of Anjou, doth take his part;
lines.plainText: Reignier Duke of Anjou doth take his part

lines.text: The Duke of Alençon flieth to his side.
lines.plainText: The Duke of Alenon flieth to his side

lines.text: The Dauphin crowned king! All fly to him!
lines.plainText: The Dauphin crowned king All fly to him

lines.text: O, whither shall we fly from this reproach?
lines.plainText: O whither shall we fly from this reproach

lines.text: We will not fly but to our enemies' throats.
lines.plainText: We will not fly but to our enemies' throats

lines.text: Bedford, if thou be slack, I'll fight it out.
lines.plainText: Bedford if thou be slack I'll fight it out

lines.text: Gloucester, why doubt'st thou of my forwardness?
lines.plainText: Gloucester why doubt'st thou of my forwardness

lines.text: An army have I muster'd in my thoughts,
lines.plainText: An army have I muster'd in my thoughts

lines.text: Wherewith already France is overrun.
lines.plainText: Wherewith already France is overrun

lines.text: My gracious lords, to add to your laments,
lines.plainText: My gracious lords to add to your laments

lines.text: Wherewith you now bedew King Henry's hearse,
lines.plainText: Wherewith you now bedew King Henry's hearse

lines.text: I must inform you of a dismal fight
lines.plainText: I must inform you of a dismal fight

lines.text: Betwixt the stout Lord Talbot and the French.
lines.plainText: Betwixt the stout Lord Talbot and the French

lines.text: What! Wherein Talbot overcame, is't so?
lines.plainText: What Wherein Talbot overcame is't so

lines.text: O no, wherein Lord Talbot was o'erthrown.
lines.plainText: O no wherein Lord Talbot was o'erthrown

lines.text: The circumstance I'll tell you more at large.
lines.plainText: The circumstance I'll tell you more at large

lines.text: The tenth of August last this dreadful lord,
lines.plainText: The tenth of August last this dreadful lord

lines.text: Retiring from the siege of Orleans,
lines.plainText: Retiring from the siege of Orleans

lines.text: Having full scarce six thousand in his troop,
lines.plainText: Having full scarce six thousand in his troop

lines.text: By three and twenty thousand of the French
lines.plainText: By three and twenty thousand of the French

lines.text: Was round encompassed and set upon.
lines.plainText: Was round encompassed and set upon

lines.text: No leisure had he to enrank his men;
lines.plainText: No leisure had he to enrank his men

lines.text: He wanted pikes to set before his archers;
lines.plainText: He wanted pikes to set before his archers

lines.text: Instead whereof sharp stakes pluck'd out of hedges
lines.plainText: Instead whereof sharp stakes pluck'd out of hedges

lines.text: They pitched in the ground confusedly
lines.plainText: They pitched in the ground confusedly

lines.text: To keep the horsemen off from breaking in.
lines.plainText: To keep the horsemen off from breaking in

lines.text: More than three hours the fight continued;
lines.plainText: More than three hours the fight continued

lines.text: Where valiant Talbot, above human thought,
lines.plainText: Where valiant Talbot above human thought

lines.text: Enacted wonders with his sword and lance.
lines.plainText: Enacted wonders with his sword and lance

lines.text: Hundreds he sent to hell, and none durst stand him;
lines.plainText: Hundreds he sent to hell and none durst stand him

lines.text: Here, there, and everywhere, enrag'd he slew.
lines.plainText: Here there and everywhere enrag'd he slew

lines.text: The French exclaim'd the devil was in arms;
lines.plainText: The French exclaim'd the devil was in arms

lines.text: All the whole army stood agaz'd on him.
lines.plainText: All the whole army stood agaz'd on him

lines.text: His soldiers, spying his undaunted spirit,
lines.plainText: His soldiers spying his undaunted spirit

lines.text: "A Talbot! a Talbot!" cried out amain,
lines.plainText: A Talbot a Talbot cried out amain

lines.text: And rush'd into the bowels of the battle.
lines.plainText: And rush'd into the bowels of the battle

lines.text: Here had the conquest fully been seal'd up
lines.plainText: Here had the conquest fully been seal'd up

lines.text: If Sir John Fastolf had not play'd the coward.
lines.plainText: If Sir John Fastolf had not play'd the coward

lines.text: He, being in the vaward, plac'd behind
lines.plainText: He being in the vaward plac'd behind

lines.text: With purpose to relieve and follow them,
lines.plainText: With purpose to relieve and follow them

lines.text: Cowardly fled, not having struck one stroke.
lines.plainText: Cowardly fled not having struck one stroke

lines.text: Hence grew the general wrack and massacre.
lines.plainText: Hence grew the general wrack and massacre

lines.text: Enclosed were they with their enemies.
lines.plainText: Enclosed were they with their enemies

lines.text: A base Walloon, to win the Dauphin's grace,
lines.plainText: A base Walloon to win the Dauphin's grace

lines.text: Thrust Talbot with a spear into the back,
lines.plainText: Thrust Talbot with a spear into the back

lines.text: Whom all France, with their chief assembled strength,
lines.plainText: Whom all France with their chief assembled strength

lines.text: Durst not presume to look once in the face.
lines.plainText: Durst not presume to look once in the face

lines.text: Is Talbot slain? Then I will slay myself,
lines.plainText: Is Talbot slain Then I will slay myself

lines.text: For living idly here, in pomp and ease,
lines.plainText: For living idly here in pomp and ease

lines.text: Whilst such a worthy leader, wanting aid,
lines.plainText: Whilst such a worthy leader wanting aid

lines.text: Unto his dastard foemen is betray'd.
lines.plainText: Unto his dastard foemen is betray'd

lines.text: O no, he lives, but is took prisoner,
lines.plainText: O no he lives but is took prisoner

lines.text: And Lord Scales with him, and Lord Hungerford;
lines.plainText: And Lord Scales with him and Lord Hungerford

lines.text: Most of the rest slaughter'd or took likewise.
lines.plainText: Most of the rest slaughter'd or took likewise

lines.text: His ransom there is none but I shall pay.
lines.plainText: His ransom there is none but I shall pay

lines.text: I'll hale the Dauphin headlong from his throne;
lines.plainText: I'll hale the Dauphin headlong from his throne

lines.text: His crown shall be the ransom of my friend;
lines.plainText: His crown shall be the ransom of my friend

lines.text: Four of their lords I'll change for one of ours.
lines.plainText: Four of their lords I'll change for one of ours

lines.text: Farewell, my masters; to my task will I;
lines.plainText: Farewell my masters to my task will I

lines.text: Bonfires in France forthwith I am to make
lines.plainText: Bonfires in France forthwith I am to make

lines.text: To keep our great Saint George's feast withal.
lines.plainText: To keep our great Saint George's feast withal

lines.text: Ten thousand soldiers with me I will take,
lines.plainText: Ten thousand soldiers with me I will take

lines.text: Whose bloody deeds shall make all Europe quake.
lines.plainText: Whose bloody deeds shall make all Europe quake

lines.text: So you had need; for Orleans is besieg'd
lines.plainText: So you had need for Orleans is besieg'd

lines.text: The English army is grown weak and faint;
lines.plainText: The English army is grown weak and faint

lines.text: The Earl of Salisbury craveth supply
lines.plainText: The Earl of Salisbury craveth supply

lines.text: And hardly keeps his men from mutiny,
lines.plainText: And hardly keeps his men from mutiny

lines.text: Since they, so few, watch such a multitude.
lines.plainText: Since they so few watch such a multitude

lines.text: Remember, lords, your oaths to Henry sworn,
lines.plainText: Remember lords your oaths to Henry sworn

lines.text: Either to quell the Dauphin utterly,
lines.plainText: Either to quell the Dauphin utterly

lines.text: Or bring him in obedience to your yoke.
lines.plainText: Or bring him in obedience to your yoke

lines.text: I do remember it, and here take my leave
lines.plainText: I do remember it and here take my leave

lines.text: To go about my preparation.
lines.plainText: To go about my preparation

lines.text: I'll to the Tower with all the haste I can
lines.plainText: I'll to the Tower with all the haste I can

lines.text: To view th' artillery and munition;
lines.plainText: To view th' artillery and munition

lines.text: And then I will proclaim young Henry king.
lines.plainText: And then I will proclaim young Henry king

lines.text: To Eltham will I, where the young King is,
lines.plainText: To Eltham will I where the young King is

lines.text: Being ordain'd his special governor;
lines.plainText: Being ordain'd his special governor

lines.text: And for his safety there I'll best devise.
lines.plainText: And for his safety there I'll best devise

lines.text: Each hath his place and function to attend.
lines.plainText: Each hath his place and function to attend

lines.text: I am left out; for me nothing remains.
lines.plainText: I am left out for me nothing remains

lines.text: But long I will not be Jack out of office.
lines.plainText: But long I will not be Jack out of office

lines.text: The King from Eltham I intend to steal,
lines.plainText: The King from Eltham I intend to steal

lines.text: And sit at chiefest stern of public weal.
lines.plainText: And sit at chiefest stern of public weal
